questions.q: Per this lesson, why should a rollout 'scope first' rather than trying to govern an entire data estate on day one?
options: A rollout that tries to boil the ocean on day one usually governs nothing well; starting scoped and expanding deliberately actually lasts
Purview technically cannot register more than one collection
There is no benefit to scoping — it's just a formality
Scoping is only relevant for very small companies
questions.explain: The lesson draws on the Thistledown Retail Group case study to argue that scoped, deliberate expansion sticks, while trying to govern everything at once tends to govern nothing well.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'scan before you classify' matters?
options: Scanning and classification are actually the exact same step
It doesn't matter which order you do them in
A classification can't flag anything in a table Purview has never scanned — the Data Map is the foundation everything else sits on
Classification rules are physically incapable of running on any scanned data
questions.explain: Classification depends on the Data Map already having scanned the source — this is why Chapter 2 preceded Chapter 3 in this course's own sequence.

questions.q: What pattern does the lesson say the 'split author from publisher' habit reflects, beyond just Purview's policy feature?
options: A rule that applies only to glossary terms and nothing else
A technical limitation that will be removed in a future Purview update
A broader governance principle: a single person shouldn't be able to both write and activate a consequential change with no second set of eyes
A requirement that only exists for Azure Storage specifically
questions.explain: The lesson generalizes Lesson 28's Policy author / Data source admin split into a broader habit worth recognizing in approvals, classifications, and workflow templates generally.

questions.q: What is this course's three-step shape, as named in its closing lesson?
options: Build it, ship it, forget it
Buy it, license it, renew it
Scan it, delete it, restore it
Find it, trust it, govern it
questions.explain: The lesson maps Chapters 1-2 to 'find it' (foundations/Data Map), Chapters 3-4 to 'trust it' (classification/catalog), and Chapters 5-6 to 'govern it' (lineage/workflows).

questions.q: Which course does the Data Governance career path continue with after Microsoft Purview, according to this lesson?
options: Advanced Databricks
Introduction to Python Programming
There is no next course — this is the final course in the entire catalog
Microsoft Fabric Data Governance
questions.explain: This lesson's closing section explicitly names Microsoft Fabric Data Governance as the next course in the Data Governance career path.
